heard: Astronauts had to cut their stations' power cables to survive. Many believe that space docking is always a safe, automated routine, like when a cargo ship docked on April 8, 1997. But on June 25, 1997, a manual docking test went horribly wrong. Commander Vasily Tzibliev lost control of the heavy-progress cargo ship. The runaway vessel crashed directly into Mir's specter module, damaging a solar panel. The violent collision punctured Mir's hull, causing a critical air leak. To save the station, the crew sealed off Spectre by cutting its power cables. This desperate cut left the station at half power, tumbling in complete darkness. This harrowing near miss proved that astronauts sometimes must cut their stations' power cables to survive.
